snapshot.description: Peerless Fence Group is the largest independently owned fence contractor in the Midwest — a 60+ year, family-founded rollup of regional Illinois/Indiana fencing businesses headquartered in St. Charles, IL, operating across Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and southern Wisconsin. Acquired January 1, 2023 by Chicago-based private equity firm Akoya Capital Partners as a Home Services platform investment, Peerless has grown through ~10 bolt-on acquisitions since 2013 and now operates its residential pipeline through Home Depot's Pro-contractor channel: leads land in HD Portal, flow into Salesforce CRM, then move to ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and accounting.
painPoints: Ashley manually rekeys every closed Salesforce quote into ComputerEase — ~1.5 hours per job (customer number, sequential job number, budget worksheet).
Daily Home Depot reconciliation: Ashley goes through HD reporting by hand to find deposit-paid status and check for new leads.
Document-by-document contract review of HS-105, 299A, 299B, HS-118 against a memorized rule set (price match, legible signatures, Friday dates, Wisconsin 99% deposit).
ComputerEase is a DOS-era legacy ERP (v26.x) with a single super-admin (Jean) and a 4-hour Deltek support SLA — a single point of failure that blocked all access changes for 2 days during PTO.
HD Portal → Salesforce is the missing wire — leads created in Home Depot Service Center don't flow into Salesforce today.

talkingPoints.trigger: When they ask why MuleSoft instead of native Salesforce Flows or a simpler tool
talkingPoints.say: The hard part of this build isn't Salesforce — it's ComputerEase. The API doesn't live on the VM's external IP and it doesn't answer on port 443 or 8081. It runs through a Deltek-managed relay service called CE Live Service that's installed on the same VM, on port 445. Brian found this during our scoping sessions. Every architect who doesn't know that detail will either hit a wall or charge you to discover it. We found it in week one of scoping before we were engaged.
talkingPoints.impact: Prevents 2–4 weeks of dead-end debugging at the ComputerEase integration layer; CE Live Service relay identification is the single biggest risk-reduction milestone in the engagement

talkingPoints.trigger: When Ashley walks through her current morning routine or describes a typical day
talkingPoints.say: The list of things that stop being your morning on go-live day is literally the scope of this proposal — UC1 kills the HD Portal check, UC2 kills the 1.5-hour ComputerEase rekey, UC3 and UC4 kill the manual contract review and the exception comment-typing on the HD screen. Your Tuesday morning changes on day one of production.
talkingPoints.impact: 1.5h/job rekey eliminated across all closed quotes on go-live day; daily HD reconciliation pass eliminated; UC3+UC4 exception review replaces document-by-document review

talkingPoints.trigger: When Brian asks about the security posture of the integration or about the GCP firewall
talkingPoints.say: The integration doesn't touch your GCP VM's external IP at all. The ComputerEase connection goes to a Deltek-managed URL — that's the CE Live Service relay architecture you identified on April 17th. Once Jean's Deltek support ticket resolves and CE Live Service gets installed, the integration endpoint is Deltek's URL, not your firewall's problem. The MuleSoft tenant IP allowlist on the GCP ingress rule is the only firewall change needed, and you've already started that work.
talkingPoints.impact: GCP perimeter security preserved; CE Live Service relay keeps the integration off the customer VM's exposed external IP; no additional firewall exposure introduced

talkingPoints.trigger: When the platform-rollout angle comes up or when Brian mentions other Elevate brands
talkingPoints.say: The architecture decisions we're making inside company code 00 today are what Brian deploys to Florida State Fence, Allied Fence, Jan Fence, and Foremost Fence. The Wisconsin 99% deposit rule in UC3 becomes a template extension — each new state adds a rule set to an existing engine, not a new build. Build it once for Peerless, run it 4 more times at marginal cost. That math only works if the Peerless architecture is designed for it from the start.
talkingPoints.impact: 5 sibling-brand deployments at template cost vs. 5 full scoping and build cycles; estimated 60–70% cost reduction per sibling deployment relative to a full engagement

talkingPoints.trigger: When the AI or AgentForce question comes up, or when Phase 3 is discussed
talkingPoints.say: AgentForce can't answer 'which Wisconsin deposits missed the 99% threshold this week' or 'which jobs are running over budget-worksheet target price' unless there's a clean Salesforce Sales Order tied to an HD F-number tied to a ComputerEase job number. Phase 1 builds exactly those joins. Without it, Ashley opens three systems and cross-references manually to get that answer — which is exactly what she does now. With Phase 1 complete, those are AgentForce queries.
talkingPoints.impact: AgentForce Phase 3 capability directly enabled by Phase 1 data joins; morning HD reconciliation and margin-watch work transferred from Ashley to AgentForce in Year 2

openingLines.line: Peerless is the Midwest anchor brand for Elevate Fence Partners' six-brand national platform — and the HD Portal to ComputerEase data path that every Home Depot Pro job runs through is the same template your five sibling brands will need when they scale. Brian has been in every scoping session making architecture decisions that are platform-standard, not Peerless-local. So we're scoping the Elevate template today, not just the Peerless instance. Ashley — walk me through what a Tuesday morning looks like, because every manual step you describe is something go-live day removes.

openingLines.context: If they say they already have a plan
openingLines.line: I'll take that and ask one question: does the plan account for the ComputerEase API not living on the GCP VM's external IP? The integration endpoint is a Deltek-managed relay URL routed through CE Live Service — not port 443, not the static IP Brian was debugging. If the plan routes to the VM directly, it'll work in a test environment and fail in production when CE Live Service isn't installed. That's the finding that changes the architecture, and we found it in week one of scoping before code was written.

Every week that doesn't start with UC2 in production is another week Ashley spends 1.5 hours per closed quote manually rekeying Salesforce data into ComputerEase — and the Elevate portfolio integration standard stays unset. Brian Cook has been in every scoping session making platform-architecture decisions. The window where Elevate's Director of IT is actively designing the template that will govern all 6 sibling company codes — and the architecture is still fluid — is the rarest deal-urgency condition we see. The template gets set once. It should be set intentionally.

openingLines.context: AI question — how does this help with AI?
openingLines.line: AgentForce works when there's a clean Salesforce object it can query — a Quote tied to a Lead tied to an HD F-number tied to a ComputerEase job number. Phase 1 builds exactly those joins. Without them, AgentForce can't answer 'which Wisconsin deposits missed 99%' or 'which jobs are trending over budget-worksheet target price before close-out' — Ashley has to open three systems manually to find those answers today. With Phase 1 complete, those questions become AgentForce queries. The Salesforce objects we define in Year 1 are what AgentForce reads. That architecture is decided once.

aiJourneyNarrative: Phase 1 turns HD Portal → Salesforce → ComputerEase into a single instrumented data path: HD Pro leads land in Salesforce within 10 minutes, 'Save as Final' quotes create ComputerEase jobs automatically, and signed HS-105/299A/299B/HS-118 contracts are validated through MuleSoft IDP. Phase 2 makes the Salesforce 'Save as Final' transition the system-of-record trigger for the whole chain — the deposit-paid box Ashley checks by hand in HD reporting syncs back automatically, and ComputerEase job status flows back into Salesforce so the team stops opening Cameo to check milestones. Phase 3 is the agentic endgame for a residential fence contractor: because Year 1 created clean Salesforce objects keyed to HD F-numbers and ComputerEase job numbers, an AgentForce agent can answer 'which Wisconsin deposits missed the 99% threshold this week' or 'which jobs are trending over budget-worksheet target price before close-out' — questions Ashley opens three systems to answer today. The Salesforce objects and MuleSoft triggers defined in Year 1 are exactly what AgentForce reads in Year 2 — that architecture is decided once, and it is the template Brian Cook deploys to all six Elevate company codes.
